correctness.rationale: A direct scalar quadratic special case gives the companion cubic. Since its value at one is fixed, reverse triangle and product bounds prove the exact global scalar minimum and force the unique triple root. The parameter-matched family has one positive real root and a conjugate pair; derivative of the exact normalized squared modulus gives a unique interior maximum at k=8/9 and factor 2/sqrt(3). Exact rational brackets certify compatibility with every cited strict sufficient condition for the 2D SPD example. Complete finite-dimensional stability threshold follows by spectral decomposition. The bundled program independently reproduces symbolic identities and 100 direct proximal updates, not replacing infinite proofs.

value.rationale: Spectral tuning based on the slowest scalar mode is a natural quantitative choice for iterative optimization. The exact 2/sqrt(3) interior rate penalty is not a cosmetic restatement: it changes which eigenmode determines the asymptotic rate, and occurs for the smallest strongly convex 2D quadratic even while all published convergence inequalities hold strictly. The unique k=8/9 location and the sharp robust q boundary give reproducible parameter-selection tests, without promising a general nonlinear theorem.
